lessons.request: think outside the box ... audit is very weak, only the looks being judged, everything needs to be judged. lessons.lesson: Argus, the auditor, checks everything a run makes, not only the looks: nothing the documents or an earlier stage hold may be lost (labelled spaces, drawn symbols, rooms, openings, pieces), every warning is read and the ones that say something was left out or fell short are acted on, the model is checked against the drawn sections, the run's own state is checked. Every finding has a problem kind, the stage that caused it and a fix; a kind that keeps coming back gets a new general rule.

lessons.question: Did Argus AI triage every finding, and was each of its fixes checked by code (target gone, nothing new broken)?

lessons.question: How many of Argus's own edits were accepted this run, and which open findings had no tool Argus could use?

lessons.lesson: Every decision and solution is general: a rule for every house, phrased for the general case, its constants with a physical or architectural reason; the project that showed a problem is only its test case. lessons.question: Does the built roof cover what the roof plan covers (every balcony, terrace or veranda under the drawn eaves, every lower roof drawn beside it), and is no outline assumed while a roof plan draws it?

lessons.request: Make argus catch these kind of things before me: the stair must lead into the floor (a pathway from the stair to the rooms)
lessons.lesson: Every stair leads into its floors: from its last step a visitor walks through a clear way of at least 0.80 m into the rooms of the floor above, and from the rooms of its own floor onto its first step; the floor opening covers only the flights, the half landing and the headroom, never the arrival floor. An assumed stair that is cut off is read the other way at build (the plan of the level above names its half landing; architect K4, the action flip_stair), and the model review's M9 reports every stair, door or floor part no walk reaches, so Argus sees it before the user does.
lessons.question: Can a visitor walk from the top of every stair into the rooms of that floor, and from the rooms onto its first step, with no floor opening across the way?

lessons.request: A throw or any cloth never shows its host through it: a cloth sunk into its host deeper than its own thickness is no rest (not built, reported)
lessons.lesson: A cloth (a throw) is measured with its own S5 tolerance (rest.REST_TOLERANCES decor_pen_cloth_m 7 mm, under its 8 mm thickness): sunk deeper, the host shows through it and it is not built (not rested, reported); a cushion keeps the soft 3 cm.

lessons.request: Give the agent loop and the big improvement loop time in every run: the regular agent rounds leave the big loop its first measure and a cycle; pod runs may take up to 180 min
lessons.lesson: AgentLoop.reserve_s (scheduler.big_loop_reserve): the regular rounds leave the big loop its first measure (10 min) and one cycle (a final round's share of the final stages + 10 min of looks); the big loop takes what is left, up to 4 cycles. Pod runs up to 180 min with --over-5-ok (user OK of 27 Oct 2026).

lessons.request: clashing sink and bath, also bath is not in proper place: drawn sanitary ware never stands in another drawn fixture; a bath read as a merged outline (bath, screen, vanity edge) is seated as a real product on its wall beside the basin, not turned across the room
lessons.lesson: Drawn fixed equipment stands where it is drawn and never through another drawn fixture (wenart/furniture/fixture_seat.py). An outline outside its type's sizes is misread or merged (a corner bath read with its screen and the vanity's edge): neither its centre nor its box angle is the piece's, so the real product is seated in it, its back on a wall and along it, covering most of the outline, clear of the other drawn fixtures and the door swings, a corner counting more. Two drawn fixtures that cut each other: the weaker reading gives way, sliding along its wall (at most 0.5 m), else seated in its drawn outline. The reading (ai_named_members, fix_fixed), the build's clash resolver (F5, the fitted model follows a new size), the architect's move_piece and Argus (a code decision from every clash left) apply it.
lessons.question: Does every drawn bath, shower, basin and WC stand on its wall, clear of every other drawn fixture?

lessons.request: correct the door (real06's entrance at the top of the outside steps: a narrow oak strip with a dark panel beside it in the opening). General rule: a library door or window fills its opening as a real product does: the catalogue box is read in the piece frame it is written in; a door or window model deeper than wide has its front along its leaf and is turned to its leaf's face; the build refuses a fit that stretches a model's width and height by very different factors; a one-leaf door takes no model wider than a real leaf (1.25 m) and none named as a pair or a sliding system: a wider entrance gets the parametric leaf with glazed side lights or a pair (D5); leaf and frame centred in the opening
lessons.lesson: A library door or window fills its opening as a real product does: its catalogue box is read in the piece frame it is written in; a door or window model deeper than wide has its front along its leaf and is turned to its leaf's face; a fit that stretches a model's width and height by very different factors is refused (the parametric opening instead); a one-leaf door takes no model wider than a real leaf (1.25 m) nor one named as a pair or a sliding system (a wider entrance gets the leaf with glazed side lights, or D5's pair); the leaf and its frame stand centred in the opening.
lessons.question: Does every outside door fill its opening as a real door: one leaf of a real width (side lights or a pair when wider), centred, never turned or stretched?

lessons.request: doors next to each other not making sense (real06's dressing room and upper hall: the AI made the windows beside the doors of two rooms doors, three doors side by side). General rule: no two doors whose openings overlap or whose frames touch (less than two frames of wall between them, or frames meeting at a corner), no two doors between the same two rooms closer than a door's width, no two swing leaves into one room that sweep over each other; a window becomes a door only for a room no door reaches and never beside the door of two rooms; the model review (M12) finds it in every project, a decision that makes it worse is refused, Argus revokes the AI decision that made such a door, and two drawn doors of one passage whose frames touch become one opening (O1)
lessons.lesson: Doors never crowd each other: no two doors whose openings overlap or whose frames touch (two frames of wall between them, none meeting at a corner), no two doors between the same two rooms closer than a door's width, no two leaves that sweep over each other; a window becomes a door only for a room no door reaches, never beside the door of two rooms; the model review (M12) finds it in every project, Argus revokes the AI decision that made such a door, two drawn doors of one passage whose frames touch become one opening (O1).
lessons.question: Does any door stand against another door (touching frames, one passage drawn twice, leaves that hit each other)?

lessons.request: Not every opening inside the house requires a door or a window. General rule: an opening between two rooms drawn with no leaf and no swing arc (a passage, an archway, an open doorway between a hall and a dressing room, a kitchen and a living area) stays an open passage: no leaf, no glass, no guard (a guard only over a drop); where the drawing is unclear the open passage is the default, a door (one solid leaf) only into a room that needs privacy (a bathroom, a WC, a bedroom); a door or passage between rooms is never made a window, a serving hatch over a drawn counter is open (no glass); the architect logs the decision (D6) and the model review (M12) reports an inside opening that got a leaf, glass or a guard it does not need
lessons.lesson: Not every opening inside the house has a door or a window: a passage between two rooms drawn with no leaf and no swing arc stays open (no leaf, no glass, no guard: a guard only over a drop); where the drawing is unclear the open passage is the default and a door (one solid leaf) goes only into a room that needs privacy (a bathroom, a WC, a bedroom); a door or passage between rooms is never made a window, a serving hatch over a drawn counter stays open; D6 logs the decision and the model review (M12) reports an inside opening that got a leaf, glass or a guard it does not need.
lessons.question: Does every opening inside the house get only what it needs: an open passage where none is drawn, a door only for privacy?

lessons.request: Tall windows where the style favours large glazing (user, 27 Oct 2026, on a Scandinavian two-storey house's renders: 'In some of the rooms the full windows from top to bottom (with a bit of remaining wall of course) could look better').
lessons.lesson: In a style family that favours large glazing (scandinavian, japandi, modern, minimal, contemporary; not classic, rustic, mediterranean, industrial) the windows of the living, dining and bed rooms (and of a dry room onto a terrace or garden) whose sill and head no document fixes become tall windows: a 0.20 m upstand to 0.25 m under the ceiling or the roof, the drawn width and position kept, all windows of one facade of the room alike; never in a wet room, never behind a wall-backed piece (a dresser, wardrobe, bed head, desk, sideboard or kitchen run keeps the sill the fit caps it at); the house's guard over a drop (W3); curtains and blinds follow the new head (architect rule W5, action tall_window).
lessons.question: Do the living, dining and bed rooms of a large-glazing style have tall windows wherever the documents fix no sill or head and no wall-backed piece stands in front, the same on every facade of the room, with a guard over a drop?
